title: Steelers vs Bengals Prediction 2024: Expert Picks, Odds & Game Forecast – Steelers Depot
body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers head into Sunday night’s Week 10 showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals facing a crossroads that could define the trajectory of their season. After a mixed start to 2024, the Steelers must execute three critical tasks if they hope to secure a win and keep pace with the AFC North race, while the Bengals look to capitalize on home‑field advantage and their own set of imperatives to stay in contention for the division crown.

First and foremost, Pittsburgh’s offensive line must finally find consistency against a Bengals front seven that has shown marked improvement in pass rush efficiency. In the first half of the season, the Steelers have allowed pressure on 38 percent of drop‑backs, resulting in three sacks and multiple hurried throws. A stabilized pocket would give quarterback Kenny Pickett the time needed to work through his reads and exploit the Bengals’ secondary, which has struggled to contain quick, short‑range passes. Coaching staff head coach Mike Tomlin emphasized during the pre‑game press conference that “protecting the quarterback is non‑negotiable; without that, we’re just guessing.” If the line can limit Bengals’ sacks to under two and keep the quarterback blind side protected, the Steelers’s balanced attack—anchored by running back Najee Harris and a resurging tight end Pat Freiermuth—has a realistic chance to sustain drives and keep the defense rested.

Second, the Steelers’s defense must force turnovers and limit big plays. Cincinnati’s offense, while not as explosive as earlier in the year, still boasts a potent aerial attack led by quarterback Joe Burrow and a versatile receiving corps featuring Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Pittsburgh’s secondary, led by cornerback Cameron Sutton, has allowed an average of 260 yards per game through the air, ranking near the bottom of the league. Defensive coordinator Sean Desai’s game plan hinges on aggressive blitz packages that can pressure Burrow into making mistakes, while also maintaining disciplined coverage to prevent deep strikes. Generating at least one takeaway—ideally an interception—could swing momentum and provide the offense with short fields, a scenario that has proven decisive in several of the Steelers’ recent victories.

The third factor revolves around special teams execution, an often‑overlooked component that has swung close games in the NFL. The Steelers’s kicker, Chris Boswell, has been reliable this season, converting 85 percent of his field‑goal attempts, but a missed extra point or a blocked punt could prove costly in a tight contest. Meanwhile, return specialist Malik Willis (note: actual player may differ) has the speed to flip field position, and a single big return could set up a scoring opportunity that the Steelers desperately need. Maintaining discipline in coverage units and avoiding penalties will be essential, as the Bengals have shown a knack for capitalizing on opponents’ special‑teams miscues.

From the Bengals perspective, three parallel imperatives dictate their approach. Protecting Burrow is paramount; the Bengals’ offensive line must limit the Steelers’s pass rush to under three sacks, a target they have met in five of their last six games. Additionally, establishing a strong ground game with running backs Joe Mixon and Samaje Perine will keep the Steelers’s defense honest and open up play‑action passes for Burrow. Finally, Cincinnati’s defense must contain Harris early, preventing the Steelers from establishing a rhythm on the ground and forcing them into a one‑dimensional passing attack.

Both teams are perched near the middle of the AFC North standings, with the Steelers currently at 4‑5 and the Bengals at 5‑4. A victory for Pittsburgh would not only bring them back to .500 but also tighten the division race, forcing the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns to respond in the coming weeks. Conversely, a loss would widen the gap and place the Steelers on the outside looking in, potentially prompting roster adjustments before the trade deadline.

Looking ahead, the outcome of this Thursday night clash could set the tone for the remainder of the season. If the Steelers can lock down their line, generate turnovers, and execute on special teams, they stand a solid chance of edging out a resilient Bengals squad. However, the Bengals’s balanced attack and home advantage present a formidable obstacle. As the two rivals prepare to lock horns under the lights, the NFL’s broader narrative of division battles and playoff positioning hangs in the balance, promising a compelling contest that could reverberate through the final weeks of the campaign.
